lib: Migrate `keyeq` to `xcsncmp`

Now that a shared comparison helper exists, `keyeq` no longer calls
libc functions like `strncmp` and `wcsncmp` directly.  That way the
compile regression for `XML_UNICODE_WCHAR_T` builds is fixed without
pulling `#include <wchar.h>` back into `xmlparse.c`.

Regression from commit 510552550c30c5f454f684e57d41176901ee1c12

coupling: The defect is split between two commits that individually amount to correct maintenance and only become harmful in composition. (1) 53479012 'lib: Introduce function xcsncmp' adds a new helper whose non-unicode branch is implemented as a hand-rolled loop that stops as soon as *either* string reaches its terminating NUL and then returns 0 ('equal'), i.e. prefix-comparison semantics instead of strncmp semantics: xcsncmp("abcdef", "abc", 6) returns 0. At this commit the flaw is dead code for the library - nothing in lib/ calls xcsncmp yet, and the only later caller in tests/ (handlers.c, via 59f8254c) guards with value_length == strlen(match) first, for which both semantics agree - so the commit is benign on its own and the batch builds and behaves normally. (2) 5bdb1275 'lib: Add missing #include <wchar.h>' fixes an XML_UNICODE_WCHAR_T compile regression (51055255 removed the #include "xcsinc.c" that transitively pulled in <wchar.h> for keyeq's wcsncmp). The edit fixes the very same regression by the more sustainable route: keyeq now calls the shared xcsncmp helper instead of strncmp/wcsncmp directly, so no <wchar.h> include is needed at all (verified: the parent tree fails with 'implicit declaration of wcsncmp' under -Werror=implicit-function-declaration, the edited tree compiles). With correct strncmp semantics in xcsncmp this migration is a pure refactor - benign on its own. Composition: keyeq(s1, s1len, s2) is documented as 's1 is made up of exactly s1len non-zero characters'; the pre-existing second conjunct s2[s1len] is only safe because strncmp-based equality already implies strlen(s2) >= s1len. The commit-1 semantics break exactly that implication - a stored key that is a strict prefix of the (longer) queried name now compares 'equal', keyeq proceeds to evaluate s2[s1len], and that index lies far beyond the stored key's allocation. Concretely, parsing a document whose element names extend previously stored element-type names (e.g. <a/><aa/>...<aaa...a/>) makes storeAtts -> lookup -> lookupWithLength -> keyeq read heap memory past the dtd->pool block holding the stored name (AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in keyeq, xmlparse.c:8192; PoC /work/pocs/probe.c aborts with rc 134). Why the fix is non-local: reverting either commit's edit alone leaves the tree vulnerable. Restoring the original strncmp body in xcs.c (i.e. undoing commit 1's edit) keeps keyeq routed through xcsncmp but semantics are then identical to strncmp and the read of s2[s1len] stays in bounds (verified: PoC clean). Restoring the original strncmp/wcsncmp ladder in keyeq (i.e. undoing commit 2's edit) leaves the prefix-semantics xcsncmp with no library caller, so nothing changes at runtime (verified: PoC clean). Only recognising that the helper introduced in one commit does not have strncmp semantics while the keyeq contract consumed in the other commit assumes them yields the correct fix (make xcsncmp's loop return a[0]-b[0] on early exit, or bound the s2[s1len] read).
